title: Tenant Eviction & Safe State Sanitization Playbook
author: Lena Ortega
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes the standard operating procedure for evicting a tenant from a Redwood Private deployment and sanitizing local runtime state while preserving forensic evidence required for customer-facing investigations and compliance. It targets operational scenarios where a tenant must be quarantined, evicted, or force-removed due to security incidents, runaway resource usage, or contract termination.

Scope
-----
- Applies to private VPC and on-prem clusters running Redwood runtime (managed control-plane or federated control-plane variants).
- Focus on tenants that host model serving endpoints: stateless inference routes, KV cache, and optional ephemeral model shards.
- Does NOT change model artifacts stored in the customer-managed model registry; this playbook deals with runtime state and telemetry preservation.

Goals and SLOs
--------------
- Safety: ensure no cross-tenant data leakage during eviction (SLO: 100% isolation for affected tenant after action).
- Timeliness: complete eviction and sanitization workflow within target windows: stateless eviction <= 120s; stateful snapshot and evidence preservation <= 5 minutes.
- Observability: retain minimal, forensically-relevant telemetry until evidence handoff (SLO: preserve 100% of request traces for the 30 minutes preceding eviction).
- Rollbackability: ability to restore tenant to previous running state from preserved snapshots (aim: successful restore in 95% of test drills).

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
| Role | Team | Contact |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Primary Incident Owner | platform-oncall (eng-sre) | #oncall-platform |
| Tenant Eviction Operator | runtime-ops | runtime-ops@redwood.ai |
| Forensics Lead | security | sec-forensics@redwood.ai |
| Customer Success (communication) | customer-success | cs-tenant@redwood.ai |

Preconditions (Quick checklist)
-------------------------------
1. Confirm authority to evict (signed PO, legal/CS approval, or incident exec order).
2. Identify tenant ID and associated control-plane cluster(s): tenant_id, cluster_id, region.
3. Confirm current model versions pinned for the tenant and object storage location(s).
4. Ensure oncall and forensics are paged; create incident artifact (ticket/CR).

When to Run This Playbook
-------------------------
- Confirmed data exfiltration or lateral movement attributed to tenant workload.
- Sustained runaway token or embedding generation causing quota or capacity exhaustion.
- Customer contract termination requiring data sanitization.

High-level Procedure
--------------------
1) Detection & Triage
   - Collect: recent traces, auth logs, process lists, network flows (last 30 minutes).
   - Snapshot current runtime state as read-only evidence (see Evidence Preservation).

2) Preflight (2–5 min)
   - Set cluster into "maintenance" target for tenant: apply routing policy to drain new requests.
   - Notify downstream dependencies and inform SRE/CS.

3) Controlled Eviction (operator action)
   - Drain in-flight requests with graceful TTL (default 10s).
   - Disable new token issuance and revoke ephemeral keys bound to tenant.
   - Terminate tenant processes and detach tenant namespaces.

4) Sanitization & Forensic Preservation (stateful)
   - Persist KV cache snapshot and token-level traces to WORM evidence bucket.
   - Clear local ephemeral caches following sanitized wipe policy.
   - Attenuate telemetry sampling to preserve forensics while minimizing PII exposure (see Telemetry section).

5) Verification & Handoff
   - Confirm tenant routes no longer receive traffic (synthetic probe).
   - Package evidence, sign with chain-of-custody metadata, notify security and CS for customer communication.

Detailed Steps and Commands
---------------------------
Note: Replace placeholders (<tenant>, <cluster>, <evidence-bucket>) with real values.

1) Snapshot signals and traces (read-only)
- Export tracing window: 30m before eviction to current time.
- CLI (internal):

  # Export traces to evidence bucket
  rwdctl trace export --tenant <tenant> --cluster <cluster> --since 30m --dest s3://<evidence-bucket>/forensics/<tenant>/$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).ndjson

2) Set routing to drain and redirect new traffic
  rwdctl routing set-policy --tenant <tenant> --policy drain --grace-period 10s --cluster <cluster>

3) Revoke ephemeral keys and service identity tokens
  # Revoke tokens issued in the last 24h for tenant
  rwdctl auth revoke --tenant <tenant> --age 24h

4) Snapshot KV cache and model state (stateful tenants)
  # Request runtime to flush and snapshot KV cache to object storage
  curl -X POST "https://<cluster>-runtime.internal/tenants/<tenant>/snapshot" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"destination":"s3://<evidence-bucket>/kv-snapshots/<tenant>/","quorum":3}'

5) Sanitize local ephemeral directories on nodes (operator)
  # Example (run on nodes hosting tenant processes)
  sudo systemctl stop redwood-tenant-<tenant>.service
  sudo rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/runtime/tenants/<tenant>/cache/*
  sudo ls -la /var/lib/redwood/runtime/tenants/<tenant>/cache/  # verify empty

Evidence Preservation and Chain-of-Custody
------------------------------------------
- Every preserved artifact MUST include the following metadata as JSON sidecar: {"tenant_id":"<tenant>","cluster_id":"<cluster>","operator":"<operator>","timestamp":"<ISO8601>","action":"tenant-eviction-snapshot"}.
- Evidence storage: use WORM-enabled object storage, bucket configured with 10-year retention for forensic artifacts.
- Hash artifacts (SHA256) and record the hash in the incident ticket.

Telemetry Attenuation Policy (for privacy & minimal exposure)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Preserve full traces and token-level metadata only for the 30 minutes before eviction. After evidence extraction:
  - Mask or redact PII fields in logs (email, API keys) using the log-sanitizer pipeline.
  - Reduce trace spans to summary-level for longer retention windows (24h -> 90d).

Sanitization Matrix (what to wipe vs preserve)
| Component | Preserve (evidence) | Wipe (post-preservation) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KV cache | Snapshot to evidence bucket | Local cache directory | Keep snapshot checksum recorded |
| In-memory session tokens | Record last token IDs | Zero out memory / terminate processes | Do not persist full token secrets in logs |
| Local model shards | Reference (artifact ID) | Remove local shard files | Model artifacts in customer-controlled registry NOT deleted |
| Network captures | Save 30m window | Rotate out/garbage collect older captures | Ensure captures are WORM-stored |

Automations and Safeguards
-------------------------
- Canary run: all tenant-eviction procedures must be exercised in quarterly drills using the sandbox tenant (tenant_id: sandbox-eject) to validate restore and evidence workflows.
- Automation hooks: use the Operator Runbook controller to run eviction steps idempotently. Example automation snippet (YAML):

  apiVersion: ops.redwood/v1
  kind: TenantEvictRequest
  metadata:
    name: evict-<tenant>-20260512
  spec:
    tenantId: <tenant>
    clusterId: <cluster>
    preserve:
      traces: true
      kvSnapshot: true
    actions:
      - drain
      - revoke-keys
      - snapshot-kv
      - sanitize-local

- Safety checks: automation will run preflight validations and fail fast if evidence bucket ACL or WORM policy is misconfigured.

Post-action Validation and Rollback
----------------------------------
- Validation tests: synthetic probe suite must return HTTP 404/410 from public endpoints and internal probe should assert no tenant process exist on nodes.
- Rollback path: if eviction was accidental, the restore sequence is:
  1. Rehydrate KV snapshot: rwdctl kv restore --tenant <tenant> --snapshot s3://<evidence-bucket>/kv-snapshots/<tenant>/snapshot-<ts>.tar.gz
  2. Re-deploy tenant service: rwdctl tenant deploy --tenant <tenant> --bundle s3://<model-bucket>/<tenant>/bundle-<version>.tar.gz --replicas <n>
  3. Remove routing drain and allow traffic after smoke tests pass.

Testing and Drill Matrix
-----------------------
- Quarterly: full eviction + restore drill on sandbox tenant.
- Monthly: telemetry export and evidence-hash verification test.
- After any code change affecting eviction paths: run GitHub Actions job: ops/eviction-integration.

Audit and Compliance Notes
-------------------------
- Retain evidence per customer contract and legal hold.
- For regulated customers, add additional encryption-at-rest keys using customer KMS and store key identifiers in sidecar metadata.

Appendix: Quick Reference
------------------------
- Minimum operator permissions: runtime-ops:evict (RBAC role), s3:PutObject for evidence bucket, kms:Encrypt for sidecar metadata.
- Common commands:
  - Check active tenants on cluster: rwdctl tenant list --cluster <cluster>
  - Force-evict (non-graceful): rwdctl tenant evict --tenant <tenant> --force --cluster <cluster>

- Contact channels:
  - #oncall-platform (pager)
  - sec-forensics@redwood.ai
  - cs-tenant@redwood.ai
